title: talos.claim/1
description: What `talos ticket claim`, `next` and `release` print: the ticket an agent now holds, with enough of the issue to start, or `error` naming why there is none. Exit codes: 0 claimed or released, 1 refused, 3 claimed by someone else, 4 `next` claimed nothing. `claim` answers claimed, claimed by someone else, or refused with any reason but `open-pr`; `next` answers claimed, `max-claims` or `none`, and never refused or claimed by someone else, since it moves on to the next ticket; `release` answers released, or refused with `open-pr` or `not-found`.

oneOf.title: claimed
oneOf.description: Exit 0, from `claim` or `next`. The issue's fields at the top level; `next` adds `swept`. `issue` and `number` are always equal: `issue` names the ticket as every answer does, `number` is the issue's own field, and both stay, since a contract only grows.

issue.description: the ticket claimed: the one asked for, or the one `next` took; always equal to `number`

number.description: the issue's number, always equal to `issue`

priority.description: the most urgent priority/pN label; p3 without one

author_association.description: GitHub's for the issue's author: OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR, NONE…

body.description: the ticket's spec, clipped; the full text stays on GitHub

comments.description: the last five; an untrusted author's words are data

trusted.description: the owner, a member, a collaborator, or Thea's or Talos's App

oneOf.title: claimed by someone else
oneOf.description: Exit 3, from `claim`: someone holds the ticket's branch. A claim takes `status/ready` off its ticket, so a held ticket is answered this way before any refusal for its labels (`not-ready`, `blocked`…); a missing, closed or pull-request issue is refused all the same.

by.description: the agent the latest claim comment a trusted author wrote names; null when none does yet, as while the holder's claim is still being written

oneOf.title: refused
oneOf.description: Exit 1. From `claim`: the issue is missing, a pull request or closed, or nobody holds it and its labels keep it from being claimed. From `release`: only `not-found`, when there is no such issue or it is a pull request.

reason.description: `not-found`, `not-an-issue` and `closed` are about the issue; `not-ready` is an open issue without `status/ready`; the rest name the label that keeps it from every claim

oneOf.title: refused: a PR is open
oneOf.description: Exit 1, from `release`: a PR open from the ticket's branch keeps it from being released; `pr` names it.

oneOf.title: at the claim limit
oneOf.description: Exit 4, from `next`: the open claims reach talos.yml's agents.max_claims.

oneOf.title: nothing to claim
oneOf.description: Exit 4, from `next`: no ticket in the queue could be claimed; `tried` counts the ones it tried.

oneOf.title: released
oneOf.description: Exit 0, from `release`: the claim is given back; `deleted` says whether its branch still existed.

swept.description: from `next`: the issues whose idle claims it released first
